trust_decision.summary: When a client connects to a Kuma Control Plane over TLS, the Control Plane's certificate must be verified against an explicitly configured CA or the system trust store; skipping verification is allowed only through an explicit opt-in (--skip-verify / skipVerify). The decision is made per connection in pkg/util/http.ConfigureMTLS for kumactl, in remoteBootstrapClient.Fetch for kuma-dp, and in pkg/intercp/client.New for CP-to-CP gRPC.

landing_point.why: The summary says kumactl does not verify the Control Plane certificate when no CA is configured; this branch is what turns a missing CA into InsecureSkipVerify, and it is the only place kumactl's ApiServerClient gets its transport (app/kumactl/pkg/client/api_server_client.go:26).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names kumactl, so a solver can argue kuma-dp is a different binary that only logs a warning and must keep working for self-signed dev Control Planes, and that pkg/intercp's nil-TLS branch is unreachable anyway because Pool.Client refuses a nil TLS config (pkg/intercp/client/pool.go:54-56) - both look like someone else's code.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An https Control Plane whose certificate chains to a system/public CA, with no --ca-cert-file (and optionally a client certificate for mTLS), must still be usable: the client must be built with system roots, not fail, and the client-cert branch of pkg/util/http/tls.go:33-39 must keep running.

O6_input_shapes: CA bundle supplied inline (kuma-dp --ca-cert / KUMA_CONTROL_PLANE_CA_CERT) -> explicit cert pool
CA file path (--ca-cert-file, read into CaCert at app/kuma-dp/cmd/run.go:236-242) -> explicit cert pool
no CA configured at all -> system trust store (previously InsecureSkipVerify)
explicit insecure opt-in from a CLI flag (--skip-verify), an env var (KUMA_CONTROL_PLANE_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY) or a config-file key (tlsSkipVerify)
persisted per-Control-Plane opt-in in the kumactl protobuf config (skip_verify field 8), reloaded for every command
inter-CP gRPC: grpcs with a TLS config vs grpcs without one (now an error) vs grpc plaintext (unchanged)
URL scheme variant http vs https in the kuma-dp bootstrap path (TLS branch only for https)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The kuma-xds-client load-test tool dials the Control Plane xDS server over grpcs with tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} unconditionally, with grpcs://localhost:5678 as its default address
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a developer/load-testing tool whose own comment says skipping verification is acceptable because it is only used for testing, so it is not a supported user entry point.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate tools/ tree, its own gRPC dial code, shares nothing with pkg/util/http or pkg/intercp

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a system-trust fallback for the DP->CP xDS channel when neither the request CA nor an xds certificate file is configured
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same trust decision on the same Control Plane connection, written by the same maintainers: caCert() already returns nil,nil when no CA is available and the template then emits a validation context with empty trusted_ca (pkg/xds/bootstrap/template_v3.go:200-215).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: make the probe HTTP client's certificate verification an explicit config switch instead of a hard-coded InsecureSkipVerify
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Identical pattern (unconditional InsecureSkipVerify behind a #nosec comment) to the three sites this fix converted to explicit opt-ins, so a security sweep would plausibly plant one here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a one-shot per-command --skip-verify override next to the persisted per-Control-Plane flag
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: kumactl already layers a one-shot flag over persisted coordinates (--api-timeout at app/kumactl/cmd/root.go:100 passed into ApiServerClient), so a maintainer could add the same layering for verification.
